script:
In Japan, you can pay a company to quit your job for you.
You contact a resignation agency, explain your situation, pay a fee—and the next morning, they call your boss and say you’re never coming back.
No awkward meeting.
No resignation speech.
No final confrontation.
The agency handles the phone calls, returns company property, and tells your workplace not to contact you directly.
And this exists because quitting can feel almost impossible in some Japanese companies.
Bosses may pressure workers to stay, delay the resignation, or make them feel guilty for abandoning the team.
So instead of facing that alone, workers simply disappear—and let a professional deliver the message.
Imagine waking up, turning off your alarm, and knowing someone else is currently telling your boss you quit.
It sounds extreme.
But in Japan, quitting became so stressful that an entire industry was created to do it for you.
title: The Great Emu War
hook_text: In Japan, you can pay a company to quit your job for you.
